publisher: AmeriCorps Office of Research and Evaluation, from the U.S. Census Bureau's Current Population Survey
vintage: 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023 (each a September survey asking about the past 12 months)
table: 2017-2023 CEV Findings: National Rates of All Measures from the Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement (data.americorps.gov view rhng-qtzw)
title: National rates of all measures, Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement
universe: Civilian noninstitutional population age 16 and over
limits: Each rate is the share of people who did the activity at least once in the past 12 months, as a fraction; the survey gives no counts of how often. Formal volunteering is through any organization (religious, school, civic, cause), not only causes; charitable giving is money or goods over $25 to a non-political group; donating to a political cause is separate. National only; state and metro rates are other tables. The download repeats the 2017, 2019 and 2021 rows; the repeats differ only in the local-election voting rate, listed under repeatedRowDifferences, and the first row of each year is kept.

use: Survey measures the cause-activity year report (scripts/research/cause-activity-year.ts) sets beside a played town's full people aged 16 and over: the share who volunteered, belonged to a group, contacted an official, donated to a political cause, attended a public meeting or discussed issues at least once in a year, against the range of the four survey years. Each counts something different from the game's act beside it (any organization, not only causes; attending, not organizing; belonging, not joining this year; a political cause, where the game's causes include civic ones), and the town's full people are not a sample of the town, so the report treats them as diagnostic proxies and draws no conclusion in either direction. Never a chance anyone reads; who acts stays each person's own scored choice.
